findings.part: quality_risk / backchain_single_pass / S-10 carve-out text: the script check as the one-pass exit's evidence
findings.claim: backchain-check does not discriminate the repaired plan candidate from the unrepaired one at the plan stage, and the D1 evidence is not a compensator for dropping passes. The one-pass exit is therefore model self-assessment with a structural floor. The draft and carve-out call it a stated, checkable exit backed by a script receipt, which overstates it.
findings.evidence: [M, my own run] I ran shiploop_backchain_graph package + validate_structure + unconfirmed_produces on the 1.16.1 run's scratch/backchain-plan files: generator-draft.json (10 steps), elaborated-candidate.json (20 steps, the pre-loop candidate) and candidate-plan.json (final). All three give ok=True, no failures, 0 unconfirmed produces. So 'check passes on the repaired candidate' is already true before pass 1. Only scratch/backchain-step-plan/candidate-plan.json fails (invariant 4, the D1 orphan). The check ships in both modes (931c53e2, 6a997a02), and 1.20.0 offers a whole loop only at plan (BACKCHAIN_NATIVE_CALLS), so one-pass changes nothing for D1. [M] F-1..F-7 in pass-01..05-log.md are all semantic (wrong supplier edge, unindexed obligation, omitted report, confirm level inspect to execute, confirm wording, lens-index gap, source label). The check models none of them. [M] The proposed text 'Report unsatisfied only for a named open gap' tells the model when to answer the one field the gate-0 runtime trusts (done() completes on exit_assessment satisfied with trivial_streak >= 0). This is a bigger conflict with the owner's 'test pass is the evidence' rule than the draft's point (4) says.
findings.proposed_change: Reword quality_risk, diagnosis and the carve-out: say the exit is model-assessed with a structural floor (unique ids, suppliers, acyclic, no orphan), not a discriminating check. Remove D1 from the 'what covers the loss' argument and attribute it to the step-plan loop. Replace I4's gate-mismatch fact with the one fact the exit actually claims: the receipt's candidate_sha256 equals the final candidate digest in the review record. Consider dropping the 'only for a named open gap' sentence so the printed text does not steer the safety valve.

findings.part: other_cuts c3 / owner_decisions D4: 'keep, one pass' against off by default
findings.claim: The draft's own evidence argues for flag-off as the smaller design, and it never weighs it. The recommendation 'pass 1 earns its time' rests on findings in an artifact the draft elsewhere says nothing consumes. The same unread-graph fact is used to discount passes 2 to 7 but not pass 1.
findings.evidence: [M] No packet in the 1.16.1 run references scratch/backchain-plan/ (grep over run/packets: 0 files). Only state.md evidence_refs lists it. pass-01-log.md says 'Changes restricted to scratch/backchain-plan artifacts ... worktree edits: none'. plan.md's only post-loop commit is Improve's 6be28af 'clarify Battleship chartroom plan'. So F-1..F-3 also stay in scratch. By contrast the step-plan graph's locator does reach the test-spec, implement and test-red packets, but 1.20.0 no longer offers that loop. [M] PLANNING_REVIEW_FOCUS already targets the classes the later passes fixed: steps that cannot be replayed, weaker-stand-in checks, wrong order, missing prerequisite or unowned verification. [M] A one-pass whole loop still pays the Until Loop wrapper. That is a host-written contract under the 9,216-byte budget (Luna overran printed budgets up to 2.6 times), about 20 min prep, a 12 min pass and the result write (about 34 min, report 2 and 3), plus the Backchain and Until Loop resource reads at plan (12 reads, 109 KB). It buys no convergence, which is the skill's reason to loop. The repo already has a one-pass read-only primitive, _BACKCHAIN_AUDIT (review/audit), at the other four stages. [I] Treating plan as an audit stage is a few-line branch in _backchain_guidance with no new prose. It removes about 480 words from the plan packet (what the owner asked: 'cut them down'). S-10 is untouched because no loop runs, and it needs no gate-0 route proof or convergence.md rewrite. It saves about 128 min at plan against 94.
findings.proposed_change: Put D4 first and present both with these numbers. Keep one-pass as the default only if the owner still chooses it after seeing them (his explicit words were 'only 1 pass'). If the flag shape is cheap, make the values one|converge|off, where off reuses the existing audit text at plan. Delete 'pass 1 earns its time' until the replay in the next finding exists.

findings.claim: Bytes changed is the wrong measure of what passes 2 to 7 caught. It hides a verification-level fix and a screen gap. By the loop's own classification four of the six later passes were non-trivial, so pass 1 had not converged. The residual a single pass leaves is concentrated in S-9 territory (a stated check that confirms each outcome).
findings.evidence: [M] pass-reports/action1..5-done-packet.json: classification non-trivial and exit unsatisfied through action 5, trivial first at action 6 (streak 1), complete at action 7. [M] pass-02-log.md F-4 changed S2's confirm level inspect to execute, which is 0 bytes. convergence.md classifies verification changes as non-trivial even when repaired. pass-01-log.md F-3 already corrected browser fixture/UI confirmation levels to execute, so pass 1 left a same-class defect. [M] pass-03-log.md: T42 applicability was missing from the selected-finding index (a lens-screen completeness gap, not a plan edit). [M] Pass 3 and 4 findings F-5 and F-6 restate AC-01 no-npm verification, which Improve review 1 had already fixed in the test strategy about 2 h earlier (report 2). That is real support for Improve covering the class, but a plausible net, not a certain one: the graph is scratch, and it is unclear that Improve opens it.
findings.proposed_change: Replace the bytes sentence in the SPEC Basis, summary and quality_risk with classification: 'passes 2 to 5 each reported a non-trivial finding: a confirm level (0 B), two confirm clauses (+422 B), a lens-index gap and a scratch source label; no edge, goal or supplier changed'. Record the accepted residual as 'an unreviewed repair of confirmation levels, relying on Improve's replayability and weaker-stand-in focus'. List nothing downstream as certain: D1-class defects have no net (Improve accepted D1 in 1.16.1 and the check is record-only), and system-test blocked in that run.

findings.claim: A cheap counterfactual exists. The 'unknown whether passes 2 to 7 mattered' and 'unknown whether Luna reports satisfied after one pass' can be measured offline before a 10 h run.
findings.evidence: [M] The pre-loop candidate is recoverable byte-exact: LEARNINGS 'Second correction' says it hashes to the freeze-log digest 9e321e3d. scratch/backchain-plan holds elaborated-candidate.json, caller-packet.json and frozen sources/. [I] One gate-0 pass on that frozen input (pass 1 took about 12 min at Luna max) shows (a) how many of F-4..F-7 a single pass finds, (b) whether the host reports satisfied under the new exit text, and (c) whether pass 1 grows. The first signal in the draft's plan is otherwise a 10 h unseeded run, and a seeded run cannot test the plan gate.
findings.proposed_change: Add a replay increment before release: copy the frozen inputs to scratch, run one one-pass Backchain cycle at Luna max (or xhigh, per D5), and log findings found against F-1..F-7, the reported exit_assessment, and the minutes. Record it in LEARNINGS as the basis of the carve-out instead of the byte count.

findings.claim: The saving attributable to this change is about 92 to 94 min (8%), conditional on three assumptions. The headline 153 and 230 figures are not this change's. Per-call thinking does not overstate the 94, because pass minutes are wall measurements that already include thinking. The change leaves the owner's actual complaint unsolved.
findings.evidence: [M] Plan loop ledger 11,15,26,18,17,12,4 gives passes 2 to 7 = 92 min. File mtimes give 15.4+25.5+18.2+19.8+9.6+5.2 = 93.7. That is 7.9 to 8.1% of 1,158.5 and 14.2 to 14.5% of 647.5. Step-plan passes 2 to 4 are 65 (ledger) or 59 (mtimes). The 153 figure needs a step-plan whole loop that 1.20.0 does not print (BACKCHAIN_NATIVE_CALLS has only plan). The 230 figure adds I2b's removal, which is unmeasured: I confirmed v1200's events.jsonl was last written 17:14 PDT, no codex exec process is running, and the task text's 'live' is wrong. Assumptions: pass 1 stays about 12 min, Luna reports satisfied after one pass (it reported unsatisfied through action 6 under the old exit text), and Improve at plan absorbs nothing (its pass 1 was 14.8 min and later passes 2.8, so one absorbed non-trivial pass costs +3 to +14). If Luna needs one extra pass the saving is about 79. About 1,064 min (17.7 h) remains, over the 10 h session timeout. Effort is the largest unmeasured lever (about 32.5% of wall clock is reasoning before short commands), and the owner's 2026-09-27 rule says E2E runs use xhigh.
findings.proposed_change: Headline 'about 90 min (8%), 0 to 94 depending on Luna's first report, about 79 with one extra pass'. Move 153 and 230 to a labelled scenario section and attribute 230 to I2b plus this change, unmeasured. Say plainly that this alone does not bring a Luna max run under the session timeout. Move D5 (effort) ahead of the build: it is a zero-code lever, and the owner's own rule says xhigh.

findings.part: increments: machinery that a normal run does not need (c2, I4, I3 wording pins, redundant missing-key check, I5)
findings.claim: Several proposed pieces are machinery relative to the request. Each can be cut or shrunk without losing the one-pass behaviour.
findings.evidence: [M] c2: the draft itself says it saves 0 if I2b holds. Repair/revise at the audit stages has never been observed on Luna. It adds about 100 words across four packets plus a conditional pin, against 'cut them down'. [M] I4: export.py loop_doc already emits 'Passes', 'Final status' and 'Trivial streak: x of y required' from the terminal receipt's progress.required_trivial_reviews, so a gate of 2 against 0 and 7 passes against 1 are already visible. A mismatch fact duplicates them. [M] Missing-key refusal: _validate_current_state already computes missing = allowed - ... - keys from _STATE_KEYS and refuses with FRESH_RUN_HINT, so adding the key to _STATE_KEYS refuses old runs without a separate _need for the key. [I] SpecCarveOutTest (asserts SPEC prose phrases) and 'each of four documents states both default two and one-pass' are wording pins, against the owner's 'test the route, not the wording'. The real-runtime route test and the converge golden are worth keeping. I5 is large (seven files, validator changes) and outside what the owner named.
findings.proposed_change: Defer c2 until a repair/revise loop is observed (convergence.md keeps default two for it). Cut I4's mismatch fact (see finding 1 for the one fact worth keeping). Drop the separate missing-key _need. Replace the two wording tests with option-name/default parity between SPEC and the code constants, and keep the vendored-runtime route test and the converge golden. Remove I5 from this plan and leave it to a later owner decision.

findings.part: I2/I3 sequencing and where the gate is defined
findings.claim: The exit wording the host copied in 1.16.1 came from convergence.md's 'Frozen plan-only child contract', not from the packet. A packet-only I2 commit leaves the tree contradictory, and the dual-mode statements in ShipLoop's docs duplicate the gate.
findings.evidence: [M] The host-written exit_condition in until-loop-start-input.json ('after two distinct complete trivial/no-change reviews since the latest reset, plus candidate-specific evidence') mirrors convergence.md's 'exit condition requiring two consecutive distinct complete trivial/no-change dependency reviews and final candidate-specific domain evidence'. The plan packet only carries the 'required_trivial_reviews: 2' sentence in _backchain_guidance. [M] Backchain SKILL.md (description 'until two consecutive trivial/no-change reviews' and 'neither substitutes for the two consecutive planning reviews') is read 4 times at plan (report 3). I2 lands before I3 in the draft, so the intermediate commit tells the host gate 0 in the packet and gate 2 in the two documents it must read. [M] shiploop SKILL.md ('Source-aware Backchain selection') and backchain-planning.md ('Source-aware native caller') restate 'required_trivial_reviews: 2'. Making them dual-mode adds a third and fourth copy of the gate (S-12: one implementation of each mechanism).
findings.proposed_change: Land the packet text, convergence.md and Backchain SKILL.md edits in one commit. In the ShipLoop docs replace the literal 'required_trivial_reviews: 2 ... two consecutive' with a pointer to the packet's printed gate, so the gate is defined once in the packet and once in convergence.md for standalone callers.
